subject: Cooking
title: The Scoville Scale: Measuring Heat
description: One-minute skill: The Scoville Scale: Measuring Heat.

hook.text: A jalapeño scores 5,000 Scoville units. The Carolina Reaper hits 2.2 million. Both are called 'hot.'

buildup.text: In 1912, pharmacist Wilbur Scoville created a test: dilute chili extract until a panel can't detect heat.

discovery.text: The number of dilutions needed becomes the Scoville rating — more dilutions means more capsaicin.

twist.text: Modern testing uses HPLC machines, not human tasters — but we still report results in Scoville units.

climax.text: Pure capsaicin registers 16 million Scovilles. Pepper spray used by police is around 5 million.

punchline.text: The hottest peppers are closer to weapons than food.

quiz.question: Who created the Scoville scale for measuring chili heat?

details.summary: The Scoville scale measures the concentration of capsaicin in peppers, from zero for bell peppers to over two million for Carolina Reapers. Wilbur Scoville created the organoleptic test in 1912 using human tasters.
details.whyItMatters: The Scoville scale provides a common language for chili heat that helps cooks choose appropriate peppers and understand the huge range of heat levels available.
takeaways: Bell peppers score zero; Carolina Reaper exceeds two million SHU
Modern HPLC testing replaced subjective human taste panels
Jalapeños range from 2,500 to 8,000 SHU as a reference point

faq.question: How was the original Scoville test conducted?
faq.answer: Scoville dissolved pepper extract in sugar water and had a panel of tasters drink increasingly diluted solutions until they could no longer detect heat. The dilution ratio became the SHU score. This subjective method varied by taster but established the concept.

faq.question: What are some common peppers and their Scoville ratings?
faq.answer: Bell pepper: 0. Poblano: 1,000 to 2,000. Jalapeño: 2,500 to 8,000. Serrano: 10,000 to 25,000. Cayenne: 30,000 to 50,000. Habanero: 100,000 to 350,000. Ghost pepper: around one million. Carolina Reaper: over two million SHU.
